Risk: Control plane outage or data loss from failure of the single management host
Threat: Hardware, disk or provider failure; bad deploy or migration
Vulnerability: Every control plane service, database and backup runs on one host (phase 0)
Existing controls: Nightly pg_dumpall; WAL archive; health checks; customer VMs keep running without the control plane
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 114 115 117 119 120 121 (phase 1 hosting: separate app, data and workflow VMs, streaming replica)

Risk: Backups unusable when needed: same host, not tested, previously unencrypted
Threat: Host loss, ransomware, silent backup failure
Vulnerability: Off-site copy not configured in production; no restore ever tested; no immutable copy
Existing controls: Nightly dumps kept 14 days; status file; age encryption before upload (feat/security-iso)

Risk: Attacker with root on the management host deletes data and backups
Vulnerability: Backups writable from the host they protect; root SSH
Existing controls: ufw default deny; NATS on WireGuard; SSH hardening (feat/security-iso)

Risk: Key person dependency: one person holds most knowledge and privileges
Threat: Illness, departure, unavailability during an incident
Vulnerability: No deputy; break-glass not defined; segregation of duties not possible
Existing controls: Runbooks in docs/; infrastructure as code (Ansible, compose)
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 6 23 122 (name deputies, sealed break-glass, documented runbooks)

Risk: Takeover of an owner/admin account at GitHub, DigitalOcean, Hetzner, the domain registrar or Resend
Vulnerability: MFA on provider accounts not verified or evidenced; shared logins possible
Existing controls: Personal accounts [to verify]
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 9 12 15 23 (hardware keys on provider admin accounts, quarterly review)

Risk: Malicious or mistaken deploy through the CI deploy key
Asset: GitHub Actions deploy secrets; management host
Threat: Compromised workflow, fork pull request, malicious third-party action
Vulnerability: Long-lived SSH key with sudo deploy.sh; deploy ran in parallel with CI
Existing controls: Fork PR guard, per-job permissions, pinned host key, tag validation, forced-command deploy user (feat/security-iso)
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 79 86 88 (branch protection, environment reviewers)

Risk: Compromised dependency, base image or GitHub Action
Vulnerability: Many npm, Go and Python dependencies; floating action tags
Existing controls: Lockfiles; pinned images in compose
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 81 87 73 80 84 (Dependabot, dependency review, SBOM, provenance, pin actions by SHA)

Risk: Cross-tenant network access in shared_bridge mode
Asset: Customer VMs and data; tenant private networks
Threat: Malicious tenant (ARP spoofing, scanning, sniffing on the shared layer 2 segment)
Vulnerability: PRIVATE_NETWORK_MODE defaults to shared_bridge: tenants share one bridge, separated by subnet and IP filter only
Existing controls: Per-VM firewall and IP filter; drop of traffic between tenant pools (feat/security-iso); production warning
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 27 133 138 (switch regions to sdn_vnet before external customers)

Risk: Container escape or cross-tenant access on shared App Platform hosts
Asset: App Platform hosts; customer apps and secrets
Threat: Malicious customer app or AI-generated code
Vulnerability: Tenants share a Docker host; previously one Docker network; earlier root command injection in the build agent (fixed)
Existing controls: Shell quoting of build input; per-app networks, cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, pids limits, optional gVisor, userns-remap (feat/security-iso)

Risk: Customer workload reaches management services (agents on 9009, NATS, host agent, WireGuard)
Threat: Compromised or malicious customer VM or app
Vulnerability: Agents listen on private addresses; CONTROL_PLANE_CIDR mis-set in the past; DOCKER-USER rules new
Existing controls: CONTROL_PLANE_CIDR 10.0.0.0/12 default; DOCKER-USER drops to private ranges (feat/security-iso); WireGuard

Risk: Interception of credentials on the platform agent channel
Asset: Database passwords, S3 keys, Kubernetes join tokens
Threat: Attacker on the tenant or provider network
Vulnerability: Agent channel is HTTP with a shared header secret
Existing controls: Agents bound to private addresses; constant-time secret compare (feat/security-iso)
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 55 68 (TLS or WireGuard to agents)

Risk: Exposure of sealed secrets through weak key handling
Asset: SECRETS_KEY / JWT_SECRET; sealed TOTP seeds, tokens, customer credentials
Threat: Leak of prgd.env or a database dump
Vulnerability: SECRETS_KEY fell back to JWT_SECRET; key in the same file as other secrets; no key ids or rotation; some customer secrets stored in plaintext
Existing controls: AES-256-GCM secretbox; HKDF sub-keys, separate SECRETS_KEY, key ids, reseal script, sealing of plaintext customer secrets (feat/security-iso)
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 56 57 58 59 63 (key-management.md)

Risk: All production secrets readable by every control plane container
Threat: Compromise of any one container (www, console, API)
Vulnerability: One environment file with every secret; API and worker read all of it
Existing controls: File mode 0600; gateway gets only its own settings
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 63 68 (split per service; OpenBao in phase 1)

Risk: Contracted engineer misuses access to customer servers
Vulnerability: Engineers in other countries with shell access during grants
Existing controls: Grants with approval and expiry; recordings; residency policy; IP allowlist; masking; offboarding with rotate-credential tickets

Risk: Engineer captures a stored sudo password through a fake prompt
Vulnerability: Gateway types the stored password into a prompt a program can imitate
Existing controls: Password redacted from recording; rotation on offboarding
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 66 67 (prefer NOPASSWD rules for specific commands; per-asset rotation)

Risk: Customer account takeover
Vulnerability: MFA optional for non-owner members; rate limiter failed open when Redis was down
Existing controls: argon2id; rate limits; MFA required for owners in production; lockout and per-email limits, fail-closed auth limits (feat/security-iso)

Risk: Staff or back office account takeover gives access to every tenant
Vulnerability: Staff are customer accounts with a flag; back office on the public hostname
Existing controls: Staff TOTP required; staff idle timeout, IP allowlist, admin tokens ≤ 24h, staff reads audited (feat/security-iso)

Risk: Console session token stolen through cross-site scripting
Threat: XSS in console or a dependency
Vulnerability: Session token in browser storage
Existing controls: React escaping; CSP for console (feat/security-iso); 24h sessions with idle timeout
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 40 41 44 (consider HttpOnly cookie sessions)

Risk: Connect AI agent performs harmful actions after prompt injection
Threat: Injected instructions in data the agent reads
Vulnerability: Agents call tools with customer credentials
Existing controls: Approvals for mutating tools and server_power; SSRF guard; secret redaction; spend caps; scoped tokens (docs/connect.md)

Risk: Customer data processed by the AI model provider
Asset: Prompts and data sent to Connect agents
Vulnerability: Data leaves to a US subprocessor when customers use Connect
Existing controls: Disclosed in subprocessor list and privacy policy; only when the customer runs agents; secret variables never sent to the model
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 127 128 (DPA and zero-retention terms with the provider, to verify)

Risk: Platform used for abuse (phishing, malware, spam, mining, attacks)
Vulnerability: New accounts can run workloads quickly
Existing controls: Prepaid gate; KYC and fraud scoring (trust module); AUP; outbound SMTP 25 blocked by default (feat/security-iso)

Risk: Payment fraud and chargebacks
Threat: Stolen cards, promo and credit abuse
Vulnerability: Card-not-present payments; affiliate payouts
Existing controls: Stripe and Moyasar fraud screening; prepaid requirement; promo code rate limits
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 35 36 (velocity rules, review of high-risk sign-ups)

Risk: Production runs with the fake payment provider or default secrets
Vulnerability: Defaults are development values
Existing controls: Ansible template sets the real provider; production refuses default and weak secrets (feat/security-iso)

Risk: DDoS against the single public edge
Vulnerability: One Caddy instance on one host; no CDN or WAF
Existing controls: Provider network filtering; rate limits

Risk: Broken authorization lets one customer read or change another's resources
Vulnerability: Authorization gaps found in review (R1-R8: SSH key scopes, project-scoped tokens, approvals escalation, SSE, firewall detach, non-public images)
Existing controls: Team/project scoping; fixes R1-R8 and tenant isolation test suite (feat/security-iso)

Risk: Exploitation of unpatched hosts or platform software
Vulnerability: No patch SLA; no host scanning
Existing controls: unattended-upgrades on the management host; patching playbook for managed assets

Risk: Attacks go unnoticed: no central logging, SIEM or alerting
Vulnerability: Logs are local Docker JSON files; no alert rules
Existing controls: Audit table; JSON access logs (feat/security-iso)

Risk: Audit trail altered to hide activity
Threat: Privileged insider or attacker with database access
Vulnerability: Audit rows could be updated or deleted
Existing controls: Append-only trigger and hash chain (feat/security-iso)
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 102 (regular export of chain heads off the host)

Risk: Supplier concentration: suspension or failure of DigitalOcean, Hetzner or GitHub stops the platform
Threat: Provider outage, account suspension after abuse complaints or payment failure
Vulnerability: Single provider per layer; no tested exit
Existing controls: Infrastructure as code; images can be rebuilt
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 122 129 130 (exit plans; backups at a second provider; abuse handling within provider deadlines)

Risk: Loss of customer VMs after a Proxmox node failure
Threat: Disk or server failure at Hetzner
Vulnerability: First node uses local LVM thin; snapshots on the same node; no off-host backup
Existing controls: RAID 1; snapshots
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 115 117 (Ceph replication, Proxmox Backup Server or Storage Box; do not advertise backups before)

Risk: Customer data left on returned or failed disks
Threat: Next tenant of an auction server; disk RMA
Vulnerability: Rented hardware returns to the provider
Existing controls: Provider states it wipes disks [to verify]
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 62 144 (wipe before cancellation; disk encryption planned)

Risk: Saudi data protection: transfers outside the Kingdom without the required basis
Asset: Personal data of Progrid Arabia customers
Vulnerability: All hosting is in Germany while region sa1 is named Saudi Arabia 1
Existing controls: Privacy policy discloses hosting in Germany; residency claim removed from the website
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 110 131 (legal review of PDPL transfer rules; Saudi hosting plan)

Risk: Late or missing breach notification
Vulnerability: No tested incident process; contacts not named
Existing controls: DPA and privacy policies state 72-hour commitments

Risk: NCA control applicability not assessed
Asset: Sales to Saudi government and regulated sectors
Vulnerability: No formal applicability assessment
Existing controls: Domain-level mapping (nca-mapping.md)
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 1 5 160 (formal NCA applicability and gap assessment)

Risk: Invoices of Progrid Arabia not compliant with ZATCA e-invoicing
Vulnerability: Phase 2 e-invoicing not built (docs/readiness-review.md A1)
Existing controls: Flag on invoices only
Planned controls (checklist IDs): — (business control: e-invoicing provider before the first SAR invoice)

Risk: Leak of Git Deploy credentials gives access to customer repositories
Asset: GitHub App private key; customer git tokens
Vulnerability: Tokens could appear in build logs; some stored in plaintext
Existing controls: GitHub App installation tokens are short lived; token redaction in build logs and sealing at rest (feat/security-iso)

Risk: Exploitation of the internet-facing terminal gateway
Threat: Attack on the WebSocket endpoint; host key spoofing
Vulnerability: Gateway faces the internet; first-use host key trust without known_hosts
Existing controls: One-time tokens; origin allowlist; certificates pinned to the gateway address; only its own settings
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 19 78 (known_hosts in production, gateway in pen test scope)

Risk: Customer DNS zones changed through the PowerDNS API
Vulnerability: PowerDNS webserver allowed from 0.0.0.0/0 on the compose network
Existing controls: API key; not published by Caddy; restriction of the API (feat/security-iso)

Risk: Staff access customer data without need
Vulnerability: Back office reads were not logged
Existing controls: Staff areas; ops masking; every back-office read audited (feat/security-iso)

Risk: Compromise of an administrator's laptop
Asset: SSH keys, provider sessions, ansible vault password
Vulnerability: No endpoint baseline; keys stored as files
Existing controls: [to verify per person]
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 143 147 148 (endpoint baseline: disk encryption, screen lock, updates, keys on hardware tokens)

Risk: Personal data kept longer than the privacy policy allows, or not deleted within 30 days of closure
Vulnerability: Purge jobs did not exist; no account deletion
Existing controls: Purge jobs and account deletion/anonymisation (feat/security-iso)

Risk: Workflow engine failure or data corruption
Asset: Temporal (auto-setup image on the app database)
Vulnerability: Development image used in production; single worker
Existing controls: Workflows retry; state in Postgres
Planned controls (checklist IDs): 72 120 (production Temporal deployment in phase 1)
